entities.summary: The Persian Constitution of 1906, was the first constitution of the Sublime State of Iran (Persia) and a result of the Persian Constitutional Revolution. It was written by Hassan Pirnia, Hossein Pirnia, Esmail Momtaz od-Dowleh, among others; and granted by Mozaffar ad-Din Shah Qajar as one of his final acts. The Constitution was also in effect during Pahlavi Iran. It is divided into five chapters with many articles that developed over several years. The Quran was the foundation of the constitution while the Belgian constitution served as a partial model, which guaranteed each citizen equality before the law, and a safeguarding of personal honour, property and speech.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Persian Constitution of 1906 established a parliamentary system and guaranteed equality before the law, safeguarding personal honour, property, and speech. It served as a model for subsequent constitutions in the Middle East.
